pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: The Arizona Registrar of Contractors uses PSI for trade-specific contractor examinations. Arizona applicants may be required to complete the Arizona Statutes and Rules Exam and a trade-specific examination depending on the license classification. Electrical candidates commonly prepare for classifications such as R-11 Electrical Residential, C-11 Electrical Commercial, or CR-11 Electrical Dual. Each classification has its own scope, requirements, and content outline. The PSI candidate information for Arizona contractor licensing explains that trade-specific content outlines identify the examination time limit, subject areas, number of items in each area, and reference materials. Candidates should study the content outline connected to the exact Arizona electrical classification they are pursuing. This is important because residential, commercial, and dual classifications may have different scopes and exam requirements. The Arizona R-11 Electrical Residential content outline lists 110 questions, a 70% minimum passing score, and 240 minutes of testing time.

pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t: Arizona electrical licensing is handled through the Arizona Registrar of Contractors rather than through a separate statewide journeyman electrician licensing board. The state licenses contracting businesses and qualifying parties for the appropriate contractor classification. Electrical candidates who want to operate as contractors or serve as qualifying parties should follow the ROC licensing path for the applicable classification. The process begins by identifying the correct license classification. Residential electrical work is associated with the R-11 Electrical classification. Commercial electrical work is associated with the C-11 Electrical classification. Dual electrical work is associated with the CR-11 Electrical classification. The selected classification determines the scope of work, required examinations, and application path. Arizona ROC applicants must complete the examination requirements for the license classification unless an approved waiver applies.

pieces.h: Open Book Test
pieces.t: The Arizona ROC electrical trade exams are open book examinations with specific reference rules. Candidates are responsible for bringing their own approved references to the examination center. Reference materials may be highlighted, underlined, annotated, and indexed before the examination session. pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t: The Arizona electrical contractor licensing process begins by identifying the correct license classification. Candidates should determine whether the intended work is residential, commercial, or both. Arizona electrical contractor classifications include residential electrical work, commercial electrical work, and dual classifications that may cover both areas depending on the license selected. After identifying the correct classification, the applicant must determine the qualifying party. Arizona requires exam requirements to be completed by the person who will act as the qualifying party for the contractor license. The qualifying party is the individual connected to the license who demonstrates the required trade knowledge and qualifications for the classification. Applicants may be required to complete the Arizona Statutes and Rules Exam. The Arizona Statutes and Rules Exam is a computer-based course and exam provided through the Arizona Registrar of Contractors. Trade-specific exams are scheduled through PSI when required for the selected classification.

pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: Arizona electrical contractor licensing is regulated by the Arizona Registrar of Contractors. The state licenses contracting businesses by classification rather than issuing a separate statewide individual master electrician credential. This means the business license classification, qualifying party requirements, and exam requirements are central to the licensing path. The R-11 Electrical Residential classification applies to residential electrical work. The C-11 Electrical Commercial classification applies to commercial electrical work. The CR-11 Electrical Dual classification is associated with both residential and commercial electrical work. Candidates should select the classification that matches the scope of work they plan to contract for in Arizona. The C-11 Electrical Commercial scope includes installation, alteration, and repair of wiring, related electrical material, and equipment used in generating, transmitting, or utilizing electrical energy less than 600 volts.

pieces.h: Test Information and Study Materials
pieces.t: Arizona electrical contractor exam preparation should be practical, organized, and repetitive. The trade exam content outlines include many of the same core topics electricians use in the field every day, but the exam environment requires fast recall and accurate reference navigation. Candidates should practice finding answers in the code book, interpreting tables, reading exceptions carefully, and applying formulas without rushing. Service feeders and branch circuits are major study areas. Candidates should review how loads are supplied, how conductors are sized, how overcurrent protection is selected, and how circuits are installed safely. Grounding and bonding is another important area that requires careful attention to definitions, conductor sizing, bonding methods, equipment grounding, grounding electrode systems, and service equipment rules. Conductors and cables, raceways and boxes, and special occupancies require repeated code navigation practice.
